name: intro
title:
Three strong resumes.
One open role.
voice: Three strong resumes. One open role. blumr helps you see who deserves a closer look.

name: 01-job
title:
Start with the job.
Stay in one place.
body: Add the title and description in quick start. Detailed setup is available when you need it.
voice: Start with a title and job description. Quick start brings the job and resumes together on one page.

name: 02-priorities
title:
Priorities when
you need them.
body: Suggested priorities are optional. Review and select the ones that matter to this search.
voice: Open the suggested priorities if you want to refine the search. Select the criteria that matter, or continue with the description.

name: 03-upload
title:
Add resumes.
Start candidate review.
body: Select resumes alongside the job description, then start the review. Assessments prepare as candidates finish.
voice: Add the resumes before saving the job. Select Start candidate review, and the candidates begin preparing in the background.

name: 04-review
title:
Evidence first.
Approval second.
body: Review supported strengths, open questions, and proposed scores before applying them.
voice: Check the strengths, open questions, and proposed scores. Your approval applies the assessment.

name: 05-candidates
title:
Direct evidence.
Transferable experience.
body: Inspect the inference, supporting passage, and question to verify. Confidence measures evidence support, not hiring success.
voice: Direct and inferred evidence are labeled separately. See why experience may transfer, its confidence, and what to verify before drawing a conclusion.

name: 06-evidence
title:
See what supports
the assessment.
body: Click a strength to open the resume and highlight the source passage.
voice: Click a strength to open the resume. The supporting passage is highlighted, so you can check the evidence and approve, correct, or flag the point.

name: 07-feedback
title:
New feedback.
A clearer picture.
body: Alex triaged scanner findings. The manager clarifies that Alex did not implement the tools.
voice: Then add what the manager learns. Alex reviewed scanner findings, but did not personally configure the tools or integrate them into delivery pipelines.

name: 08-proposal
title:
Understand what
changed—and why.
body: blumr explains the new evidence and proposes an updated assessment. Current scores wait for approval.
voice: blumr explains how that new evidence changes the assessment. The proposed update stays separate from the current score until you approve it.

name: 09-lesson
title:
Learning without
extra steps.
body: Eligible patterns from repeated, consistent feedback carry into relevant searches automatically. Custom lessons are optional.
voice: Qualifying patterns from repeated feedback apply automatically to relevant searches. Current requirements take precedence. Custom lessons remain optional.

name: 10-shortlist
title:
A more informed
shortlist.
body: Review the updated picture and decide who to speak with next.
voice: Return to the candidates with a clearer picture of the experience behind each assessment.

name: 11-submittal
title:
A concise draft.
Ready for your edit.
body: Prepare a short submittal built from the candidate’s supported strengths. Review, edit, and copy.
voice: When you are ready, prepare a concise submittal from the candidate’s supported strengths. Review it, make it yours, and copy.

name: outro
title:
Less time reviewing resumes.
More time engaging
the right people.
voice: blumr. Intelligence. Unlocked. Built by recruiters, for recruiters.
